why: The documented P2/P3 boundary (roadmap §3.2 row 7), now on the P3 side of it: `my $log = Shop::Log->new; $log->write` resolves via P3's typed-receiver rule (a file-local constructor-assignment map); `$thing->write` on an untyped parameter has no declared type to resolve from and stays a permanent miss. `Shop::Log->new` itself (a qualified-receiver call, §3.2 row 3) is unrelated to this boundary and resolved back in P2 — this case's job is to prove P3 resolves exactly the literal-constructor shape and nothing more.
